design: Learned conditional world model serving Monte Carlo leaf evaluation. Object: a generator G_theta(r_{t+1..t+h} | x_t) of the joint multi-asset forward-return path on the PIT daily Kraken panel (~273 assets, true UTC daily bars from trader/data.py, market-residual and vol-standardised returns as in the memo's target), conditioned on a 60-day OHLCV window; three estimator arms — (a) closed-form conditional Gaussian/copula baseline (HAR-RV or Yang-Zhang conditional vol, Ledoit-Wolf/DCC covariance, mean = ridge), (b) neural conditional flow/diffusion or RSSM (Dreamer/PlaNet class) over 21-day x N-asset blocks, (c) Bella re-conditioned on the window (TASK_722/778 ansatz). Use: for a candidate book w the leaf is V_K(w) = (1/K) sum_k u(w . r^k - c|w - w_prev|) over K rollouts; the planner is either the existing Gumbel/sampled search with this leaf (the 828 operator with pw0.0, E5-inversion3 shape) or sample-average-approximation of the Garleanu-Pedersen program on the same scenarios. NOTE the resident Bella cannot serve this as-is: it is a minute-bar generator (reads the `ohlcv` minute table, diff_teacher/data_loader.py:182-190), trained on 64 SURVIVOR assets only (`WHERE a.is_active = 1`, data_loader.py:151-157), window 400 steps (diff_teacher/CLAUDE.md:8-9), checkpoint actually 768d/12L + 10 ODE steps not the documented 1536d/16L (lore/notes_2026-05-18.md:84-86), `generate(seq_length=1440)` broken by a pad bug (notes_2026-05-18.md:79-83), and its paths measured ~7x too easy (oracle PnL 0.0124/step vs 0.0017 historical, notes_2026-05-18.md:87-96). A daily-surface generator is a new build, not a Bella reuse. The inventory/cost half of the transition is NOT learned: PnL = w . r and fees are known exactly (jax_trading_env.py:1621-1820 per memo), so the leaf's action-conditionality is exact by construction — the only learned component is the price law.
what_the_loop_learns: The learned object is the conditional law P(r_{t+1:t+h} | x_t), which decomposes into (1) the conditional mean mu(x) — identical in content to what a supervised forecaster / the memo's IC instrument estimates, but estimated with MORE parameters spent on nuisance dimensions (marginals, dependence, tails), hence with higher estimation variance for the same data; a likelihood-trained generator recovers E[r|x] only as a by-product, never better than a regression targeted at it; (2) the conditional covariance Sigma(x) — vol level, vol clustering, cross-sectional correlation/N_eff and its regime dependence; (3) higher-moment shape — skew, kurtosis, tail co-movement; (4) temporal dependence within the horizon — persistence of vol regimes, autocorrelation structure of the path. Beyond a direct estimator it carries ONLY (2)-(4) jointly and coherently (a scenario set with the right joint dependence rather than separate point estimates). Why those exist in daily OHLC on Kraken: volatility clustering and range-based vol predictability are the most robust stylised facts in crypto (HAR-RV forecasts of BTC RV have out-of-sample skill; Parkinson/GK/Yang-Zhang range estimators are 5-8x more efficient than close-to-close — memo A-2, never used in-repo); cross-sectional correlation to the BTC factor is persistent and regime-dependent. Which of these can create EXPECTED profit under the goalposts (Sharpe, BEAR-positive, 21 bp/side): exactly none except (1). Proof by iterated expectations: for ANY causal position process w_t measurable w.r.t. the information set F_t (which contains everything the generator conditions on), E[gross] = sum_t E[w_t . r_{t+1}] = sum_t E[w_t . E[r_{t+1}|F_t]] = sum_t E[w_t . mu_t]. If mu_t = 0 a.s., expected gross is zero for every rule, however perfectly Sigma, tails and persistence are known; net is minus turnover x 21 bp. Path-dependence within the horizon does not escape this: a multi-step strategy's gross is the same sum with w_{t+j} measurable at t+j, still requiring a nonzero one-step conditional mean at SOME information set. Second-moment knowledge changes expected profit only through one channel: volatility timing of a book that already has drift (Moreira-Muir: Sharpe rises because expected return does not scale with variance) — it re-times a premium, it does not create one, and vol-timed long-only crypto is not BEAR-positive. Everything else the generator carries (tails, dependence) affects variance, drawdown and turnover — the denominator and the cost term — not the numerator.
worth_if_ic_is_zero: Zero as an alpha object; negative as a planner leaf; positive only as a null-distribution engine. Mechanics: the MC leaf for book w averages to V_K(w) = w . mu_G(x) - c|dw| - (gamma/2) w' Sigma_G(x) w + O(sigma_w / sqrt(K)). With true mu = 0, mu_G(x) is pure estimation noise (the generator's fitted drift on a signal-free target, with at least the variance of a ridge fitted to the same target). Argmax over books is then w = 0 (HOLD) if the risk term dominates, or noise-driven trading if it does not — the two measured attractors exactly (887 adaptive HOLD at zero cost; 892 anti-edge vs matched coin flip, delta -0.043..-0.056 with every CI < 0, LEDGER row 892/action-ev). Magnitudes: a 60%-vol book has sigma_w ~ 3.5%/day; at the goalpost IC 0.02 the daily expected book return is ~IC x sigma_book ~ 7 bp; MC noise at K=256 is 3.5%/16 ~ 22 bp per leaf, so even an INFORMATIVE mu_G is swamped by rollout noise unless K >~ 2500 per candidate per decision, whereas the closed form uses mu_G directly with zero MC noise — the record already shows leaf noise converting to churn and fees (E5-inversion2 true-env leaf at fee16: -4.88/-1.44 with hold 55-68% vs pure-Q +8.02 with hold 94.2%, LEDGER rows 832/E5-inversion2, E5-inversion3; K>32 declines monotonically as turnover tax, 831x/D). The record's +8.02 (E5-inversion3) is the value of a leaf whose 'mu' is the REALIZED 3-day path (per-decision IC = 1, in-sample); a causal generator's leaf has 'mu' = E[r|x] with IC <= the ceiling the memo's instrument measures; the gap 0.03 -> 1.0 in leaf calibration (849/leaf v-hat +0.03) is the gap between a conditional expectation and a realised outcome and no generator trained on the past can close it. What survives at IC ~ 0: (i) a generator with mu forced to 0 but realistic vol clustering, cross-correlation and tails is the CORRECT null distribution for the IC instrument itself — it replaces the memo's 'max of four label shuffles' noise floor (memo E-2, cap_aggregate.py:46-57) with a calibrated 'no conditional mean, realistic dependence' null; (ii) variance/tail forecasts still cut turnover and drawdown of whatever book exists (worth ~0 Sharpe on a zero-drift book, ~+0.1..0.2 of drag on a book with drift).
measured_failure_mode_and_escape: Two measured failures bind. (A) 849/leaf: the learned value leaf is action-blind (v-hat Pearson +0.03 vs true one-step reward, r-hat +0.29; prior selected in 4.5% of states) so search rationally avoids fee-paying candidates -> HOLD/churn attractor (LEDGER row 849/leaf; the 857/860 distill lane could not lift deployed-Q past +0.31..+0.38 against a +0.5 steering bar and 879/rung3 shows the search stack subtractive, delta 1.602). ESCAPE, mechanical: in this design the leaf is not a learned v-hat(s,a); it is an MC expectation whose action-dependence enters through the KNOWN inventory/cost dynamics (PnL = w . r, fees linear in |dw|), so leaf sensitivity to the action is exact by construction — the same mechanism that restored action-sensitivity when the true env replaced the learned leaf (E5-inversion2/3) and that 834/E3-p1b already achieved for the reward head (R_model 1.30/1.12 vs bars 0.33/0.24). This half is genuinely escaped. (B) 887/collapse-confirm + 892/action-ev: the HOLD fixed point is ADAPTIVE — at zero cost, hold 99.0% loses 2.9%, 95.7% loses 9.1%, 91.2% loses 13.8%, monotone in activity — because the actions have negative EV; the imprint's OOS actions are worse than a matched coin flip. ESCAPE: none by mechanism. By the iterated-expectations identity the design's expected gross is sum E[w_t . mu_G-implied direction x true mu_t]; if true mu ~ 0 the generator leaf reproduces exactly the 887/892 outcome (argmax w=0, or noise-trading that pays fees). The only escape is the hypothesis that the generator's implied conditional mean carries market-residual IC >= 0.02 that survives 2024-2026 — i.e. that it IS a forecaster — which is the memo's G-A gate, not a property of the loop. Corollary: the design cannot be a way AROUND measuring the IC ceiling; it is downstream of it. Third failure it must also avoid: 758's sim-to-real gap (Bella paths 7x too easy; a planner trained/evaluated inside such a generator learns 'Bella-shaped' policy, notes_2026-05-18.md:96-100) — escaped only by the oracle-PnL-ratio disqualifier in the kill experiment, not by any property of MC rollouts.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: BEAR-positivity requires E[w . r] > 0 on a window where the market factor's mean is negative. With mu(x) = 0 every causal book has E[gross] = 0 (iterated expectations), so no scenario-MC planner, however well it knows Sigma(x), tails or regime persistence, has positive expected return in BEAR22 — its expected net is -turnover x 21 bp. The only forecast-free positive channel a second-moment model offers is vol-timing of a risk premium (Moreira-Muir), and the crypto premium is long-market beta: the repo's own measurements show long-only constant mix gross -0.40 FULL / -2.54 BEAR22 PIT and long-flat trend 2026H1 -5.221 (tactics panel lines 79-81, 36; LEDGER 898/trend-decay). The record's only BEAR-positive behaviour is the trend book's short leg (BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat -2.471), which is a forecast. A generator could be BEAR-positive only via its implied conditional mean on market-residual returns — that is a forecast by definition, so the answer is 'no' rather than 'conditional'.

literature.ref: Yu, Lee, Kulyatin, Shi, Dasgupta 2019 — Model-based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Portfolio Optimization (arXiv 1901.08740)
literature.claim: The 'model-based' gain is a supervised-forecaster gain: the infused prediction module (NDyBM / WaveNet-style next-return predictor) supplies the lift; data augmentation (GAN) adds ~0; test window is 23 months, single run, no CIs.
literature.numbers: 6 US equities + cash, S&P as feature; train 2005-01-01..2016-12-31, test 2017-01-01..2018-12-04; fees 20 bp + 50 bp slippage; Table 1 (DDPG): Sharpe CRP 0.57, baseline 0.56, IPM 0.61, DAM 0.57, all modules 0.63; ann. return 7.25% vs 8.09%; MDD 13.10% vs 12.40%. Table 2 (PPO): baseline 0.37, BCM 1.13, IPM+BCM 1.26.

literature.ref: Aghapour, Bayraktar, Yuan 2025/26 — Dynamic data generation and dynamic portfolio selection: an application of a score-based diffusion model (arXiv 2507.09916v4)
literature.claim: Closest published instance of 'conditional generator -> policy trained in generated environment'. Beats history-based Markowitz and equal-weight, but long-only, fully invested, monthly, NO transaction costs, fixed seed, no CIs — beta-loaded and not bear-positive; the generator-fed Markowitz gain comes with much higher vol, consistent with the generator supplying a (momentum-like) conditional mean, i.e. a forecast.
literature.numbers: FF-10 monthly industry portfolios, 15-stage annual walk-forward 2010-03..2025-02 (180 decisions), gamma=3, zero reference rate: Sharpe S&P 0.818, EW 0.883, HistMarkowitz 0.789, GenMarkowitz 0.925 (vol 21.71% vs 16.71%), HistTD3 0.552, GenTD3 1.225 (ann. 18.79%, MDD -15.71%). FF-30: EW 0.739, HistMarkowitz 0.733, GenMarkowitz 1.045, GenTD3 1.096. 'exclude transaction costs' stated for both experiments.

literature.ref: Liu, Zong et al. 2026 — Bayesian Robust Financial Trading with Adversarial Synthetic Market Data (arXiv 2601.17008)
literature.claim: Synthetic data used as adversarial training augmentation for single-instrument long/short/flat DQN-class agents, not as a rollout leaf; no synthetic-to-real gap quantified; no seeds/CIs; fee rate not stated in the scanned text.
literature.numbers: 9 ETFs, test 2021-2024; Table 1 Sharpe e.g. FXY: Ours 2.51 vs Buy-and-Hold -1.73, DQN 1.39; DBC: Ours 1.34 vs B&H 0.99; FXB: Ours 1.07 vs B&H -0.49.

literature.ref: Buehler, Horvath, Lyons, Perez Arribas, Wood 2020 — A Data-driven Market Simulator for Small Data Environments (arXiv 2006.14498)
literature.claim: Market generator (VAE on log-signatures, S&P daily) is evaluated by signature-MMD two-sample tests; deep hedging is discussed as a connection ('unrealistic training data can lead to large losses') but the paper reports NO train-on-synthetic/test-on-real hedging P&L numbers — the sim-to-real gap for generator-trained policies is asserted, not measured, here.
literature.numbers: Evaluation tables are MMD/signature comparisons (weekly/monthly path level); no Sharpe or P&L figures.

literature.ref: Ni, Szpruch, Wiese, Liao, Xiao 2020 / Liao et al. 2024 — (Conditional) Sig-Wasserstein GANs for time series generation (arXiv 2006.05421; Math. Finance)
literature.claim: Defines conditional generation of the future path given the past under a signature-W1 metric; reports distributional fidelity (marginals, correlations, ACF), not trading P&L on real data.
literature.numbers: S&P 500 / DJI daily 2005-2020; Sig-WGAN improves WGAN on correlation and marginal metrics with reduced training time (no P&L).

literature.ref: 'Beyond Visual Realism: Toward Reliable Financial Time Series Generation' (SFAG) 2026 (arXiv 2601.12990)
literature.claim: Standard GAN/WGAN-GP synthetic series yield implausible strategy backtests; only structure-preserving constraints give backtest-valid paths — the generic form of the repo's own 758 finding (Bella paths 7x too easy). A planner evaluated inside a generator inherits the generator's artefacts as 'edge'.
literature.numbers: Shanghai Composite 2004-2024; baseline GANs produce annualized returns exceeding 2000% in backtests; SFAG momentum 27.8% ann. return, 9.37% vol.

literature.ref: Model-based RL with non-Gaussian environment dynamics and its application to portfolio optimization (arXiv 2301.09297)
literature.claim: Heavy-tailed normalizing flows as the learned dynamics; claims lower max drawdown in COVID period on Dow/NASDAQ/S&P stocks; no numbers or cost model in the abstract.

literature.ref: Moreira & Muir 2017 JF — Volatility-Managed Portfolios (+ Cederburg et al. 2020 as cited in the tactics panel)
literature.claim: The ONLY channel through which a second-moment model raises Sharpe: scaling exposure by 1/variance works because expected return does not scale with variance — it re-times an existing premium and creates none; Cederburg et al. find the gain significant for 8/103 strategies, MOM the exception.
literature.numbers: vol-managed momentum 'nearly doubles' Sharpe (Moreira-Muir); Cederburg MOM 0.48 -> 0.99, 8/103 significant.

literature.ref: DeMiguel, Garlappi, Uppal 2009 RFS — Optimal Versus Naive Diversification
literature.claim: Moment-estimation error dominates optimisation gains out of sample; scenario-MC/CVaR optimisation with generator-estimated moments is a worse-conditioned instance of the same problem (CVaR errors carry mean AND covariance error).
literature.numbers: 14 models on 7 datasets, none consistently beats 1/N in Sharpe, CEQ or turnover.

literature.ref: Dreamer / DreamerV3 (Hafner et al.) applied to trading
literature.claim: No peer-reviewed Dreamer/world-model trading result with out-of-sample net-of-cost Sharpe was found in three searches; DreamerV3's gains are in controlled MDPs where the action changes the transition — absent here (price exogenous, inventory dynamics known).

literature.ref: Conditional Generators for Limit Order Book Environments: Explainability, Challenges, and Robustness (arXiv 2306.12806)
literature.claim: Conditional GAN market environments show exploitable dependence on input features under adversarial probing; realism and robustness must be engineered — a documented sim-to-real hazard for RL-in-generator training.

honest_use: Three bounded roles, none of which claims expected return. (1) Null-distribution engine for the predictability-ceiling instrument (memo §4): fit the conditional generator on the PIT panel with the drift term constrained to zero (or with returns sign-randomised per (date, asset) after fitting), generate M>=200 placebo panels that preserve vol clustering, cross-sectional correlation, N_eff and tails, and re-run the full 160-cell IC sweep on each — this yields the Bonferroni/NW-corrected IC threshold under 'realistic dependence, no conditional mean' instead of the memo E-2 'max of four shuffles' floor. CPU/one 24 GB card, hours. This is the one use where the generator supplies information a direct estimator cannot. (2) R4 stress generator (D5's stated role): scenario-MC evaluation of a CANDIDATE book (the GP book if G-A passes; the tactic library otherwise) — CVaR and drawdown distributions under Sigma misestimation, correlation spikes, vol regime shifts; estimation-error-aware sizing (fractional Kelly / shrinkage of the aim portfolio) and a conditional-vol-scaled no-trade band. Expected effect: on a book WITH drift, ~-17% turnover at equal Sharpe (Yang-Zhang vs close-to-close, Baltas-Kosowski via the panel) and +0.1..+0.2 Sharpe of cost/variance drag; on a zero-drift book, 0 — it cannot make net@21 positive and cannot make a book BEAR-positive. Must be scored on trader/ with simple returns and drift-inclusive turnover (panel corrections 2-3). (3) Execution-style calibration for a daily rebalance (limit vs market), downstream of the 907 estimands — second-order per memo §1.4. Explicitly NOT a legitimate use: as the value leaf of a trading search, as a policy-training environment (758's 7x ratio; SFAG's >2000% GAN backtests), or as a way to bypass the IC gate.
compute: Daily-surface generator: ~273 assets x ~2000 days = 550k asset-days; a conditional flow/diffusion or RSSM over 21-day x 273-asset return blocks with a 60-day context is O(10^7) parameters, trains in hours on ONE 24 GB card (arm (a) closed-form conditional Gaussian/HAR/Ledoit-Wolf is CPU-minutes); ~20 quarterly expanding-window refits x 4 horizons <= 1 GPU-day. Rollout leaf: K=512 x 21 days x 273 assets per candidate x ~900 OOS decisions is trivial (seconds per decision on CPU). Null-panel generation (M=200 panels) is CPU-hours. 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to any of this; they matter only for (i) a minute-scale multi-asset generator (Bella-class 300M+ params over 1440 steps x 64+ assets, or the full 1193-asset panel) or (ii) Dreamer-style end-to-end RSSM + actor-critic self-play with long imagination horizons at high batch — and the minute surface is closed at any nonzero fee (897: 0/864 cells) while imagination-trained policies are the 887/892 loop with a learned simulator in place of the real one. Before the IC ceiling is measured no GPU beyond the <=1 GPU-day kill experiment is warranted; the 64 GB cards should not be justified by this design.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered, SPEC sha256 recorded before the first fit, run on the SAME PIT daily panel, dates, purge and quarterly expanding-window schedule as the memo's §4 IC instrument (true UTC daily bars via trader/data.py, market-residual Yang-Zhang-standardised target y_{i,t,h}, h in {1,3,7,21}). Arms: G0 = conditional Gaussian baseline (mean ridge on F1-F3, HAR-RV/Yang-Zhang conditional vol, Ledoit-Wolf covariance); G1 = neural conditional flow/diffusion (or RSSM) with a 60-day OHLCV context, no volume if unavailable; G2 = Bella re-trained on daily bars (optional, only if G1 passes stage 1). At each test date sample K=512 paths, compute mu_hat_G(x_t) (rollout mean, residualised and standardised identically to the instrument) and Sigma_hat_G(x_t). Stage 1 (alpha content): per-date cross-sectional Spearman IC of mu_hat_G vs realised y, by year 2024 / 2025 / 2026H1, Newey-West lag h, PAIRED against the ridge and GBM IC on identical dates (block bootstrap of the daily IC difference). Stage 2 (second-moment content): QLIKE and Mincer-Zarnowitz R^2 of sigma_hat_G^2 vs realised variance from the minute cache, paired Diebold-Mariano vs HAR-RV and trailing-30 Yang-Zhang. Stage 3 (does the wrapper add anything): feed the SAME mu_hat, Sigma_hat to (i) Garleanu-Pedersen closed form and (ii) the MC-leaf search at K in {16, 64, 512}; grade both with unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics net@21 and eval_vector --operator policy-argmax with the pinned frame. Stage 4 (sim-to-real disqualifier): the 758 metric — per-step oracle PnL ratio on generated vs real paths — must lie in [0.7, 1.4] and generated-path momentum/reversal backtests must match real within bootstrap CIs, else the generator is disqualified before Stages 1-3 are read.
kill_experiment.instrument: experiments/9xx_ic_ceiling/ runner (shared with the memo's instrument, so the generator cells are extra columns of the same 160-cell grid, not a new grid); trader.backtest.cell_metrics (seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21) for the PIT engine read; eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance with pinned frame for the in-env read (the 882/decisive-legA two-instrument discipline); the 758 oracle-PnL-ratio harness (experiments/758_bella_augment/SPEC.md 'too_easy' protocol) for Stage 4. open_doubts: The iterated-expectations identity binds any causal rule, but the RELEVANT conditional mean is E[r | F_t] for the generator's information set. A learned 60-day multivariate encoder could in principle expose a conditional mean the memo's fixed feature families F1-F4 miss (functional-form or interaction structure). The signature arm F4 and the GBM arm are the hedge, and 811/819 CAPACITY say nonlinear <= linear, but 819 CAPACITY is pre-E-c, 20 assets, close-only — a weak instrument for this specific doubt. Stage 1's paired IC test is the direct check.

The by-year mean IC gate can miss edge concentrated in a few regime-days (a generator's conditional mean might be near zero on average and large in high-dispersion states). Remedy inside the kill experiment: report IC conditional on generator-implied vol/dispersion terciles; not a reason to skip the gate.
